Elena / Nimbus legal team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As discussed, Nimbus is confirming an incremental uplift to the orderbook as part of the upcoming 12-month renewal. High-level items we need to land with your counsel for the signature packet:

- MSA: small indemnity cap rewording requested in §9; your teams asked to move from a fixed cap to a three-month subscription average — Redwood legal queued a proposed alternative.
- Order form: convert the seat-based pilot into a throughput/requests-based addendum (see attached spreadsheet for proposed mapping).
- Data retention & access: your security team requested explicit wording for log retention and audit access (SOC2 evidence stub attached).
- Effective date / term: Nimbus prefers aligning the effective date to 2028-08-01 with a 12-month term and a 30-day invoice cadence.

Action items I propose for today:
1) Nimbus legal: send your redline of the attached MSA (minor language changes only) and confirm acceptance of throughput metrics mapping.
2) Redwood (Ben / Mateo): prepare a clean order form with the throughput addendum and a short cover note that explains how burst capacity will be billed.
3) Both legal teams: quick 30-min sync tomorrow to confirm indemnity language and data-retention text.

I’ve attached our working redline and the order mapping. If nothing major, we can bundle for DocuSign once legal has the indemnity language agreed.

Thanks —

Kimberly —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. I’ve looped in our general counsel (legal@nimbushealth.com) and procurement. A couple quick notes from our side:

- Indemnity cap: we do want the cap tied to a lookback metric as discussed; legal will send a short redline suggesting "greater of three months' fees or $250,000" instead of a flat multiple.
- Throughput addendum: procurement has reviewed your mapping and flagged two burst rules that need clarification (how bursts prorate across months).
- Audit access / SOC2: legal accepts the evidence stub but requests a clause that limits redwood's obligation to provide full-prod logs to cases with a signed NDA.

We’ll get a redline back by end-of-day Wednesday from our counsel with comments inline on the PDF. If Redwood can confirm the billing note for burst handling before the EOD, procurement will prepare a PO template so accounting can expedite.

Best,

Kim / team —

Quick update from our side after reviewing Nimbus's early redline:

Summary of proposed changes we will push back on / clarify:
- Indemnity cap tweak: Redwood legal proposes a compromise: "cap equals the greater of six months' average invoiced fees or $300,000" — rationale: protects against noisy monthly variability for throughput billing. We can present both options at the legal sync.
- Burst prorating: standard approach we use is to bill actual burst usage over threshold at the end of billing month with a 1% rounding tolerance; Ben suggests we add an example table into the addendum so procurement sees the math.
- NDA gating for logs: we accept the NDA gating but suggest an internal SLA for turnaround on evidence requests (3 business days) — otherwise large customers create operational drag.

Attached is a proposed clean order form and a one-pager that shows how monthly throughput maps to the seat-rate equivalent. I also added a short illustrative table for burst prorating.

Next steps:
- Mateo to coordinate with Redwood legal to finalize the indemnity counter-proposal and circulate before the Friday sync.
- Kimberly to confirm if finance will accept a 30-day invoice cadence or if Nimbus needs 45 days for procurement lead time.
